description.narrative: REFs, d.v.s. Roma Education Funds, verksamhet syftar till att höja utbildningsnivån för romer i Europa. Sida avser ge kärnstöd till REF, vars verksamhet består i att genom projektbidrag, stipendier, forskning och påverkansarbete öka antalet romer som får kvalitativ utbildning från förskola ända upp till doktorsgrad. Sida avser finansiera verksamhet i alla de ODA-klassade länder som REF är verksamt i, d.v.s. i Albanien, Bosnien Herzegovina, Kosovo, Makedonien, Montenegro, Serbien, Turkiet, Moldavien och Ukraina. Sida har i flera år gett projektstöd till REF men bedömer nu att REF som organisation är mogen att hantera kärnstöd. REFs kapacitet att hantera medel på ett ansvarsfullt sätt samt organisationens förmåga att bedriva sin verksamhet gör att Sida bedömer den sammantagna risken för insatsen vara låg.

Roma Education Fund, REF, aims at increasing the level of Education of Europe's Roma population. Through the means of providing project grants, scholarships and through research and policy work REF contributes to increase the number of Roma achieving qualitative education at all levels in the education cycle, from pre-school to post-graduate studies.
Distribution: No country allocations in advance.

To close the gap in educational outcomes between Roma and non-Roma. REF contributes to SDG 4 - ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all. The REF strategic framework 2021 - 2030 sets out three strategic orientations: i) supporting individual beneficiaries,ii) utilizing/sensitizing education systems through advocating the needs and interests of Roma,iii) making REF a specialised organisation for the mobilization of the human potential of Roma and their contribution pedagogy.

Roma Education Fund (REF) has worked to develop models in five activity areas of supporting Roma education and worked to institutionalise the use of these models by the local authorities in the region. Through this working method REF has become one of the main drivers of stimulating initiatives aimed at ensuring equal opportunities in education and the educational inclusion of the Roma population. This could for exampel be seen in the meta-analysis of interventions for Roma inclusion commissioned by the European Commission, where a substantial part of the interventions taken into consideration were supported by REF. Specifically REF worked against the segregation of Roma students in special classes and as a results there was a 15 percent decrease of segregation of Roma students, in the countries where the representation of Roma children in special schools was significant.
Examples of the results in the Balkan countries include:
Serbia -Roma children dropout rate in Serbia was reduced from 7% to 2.4% (2014/15-2018/19) -The number of high school graduates increased from 98 to 148 annually (2014/15-2018/19) -The Institute for Improvement of Education of the Ministry of Education, Science and Technological Development of Serbia accredited Module 3 The Role of Mentors in Strengthening Life Skills and Competencies Essential for the Employment of Scholars a total of 251 mentors passed three courses designed and accredited by REF (2015/16-2019/20).
Bosnia and Herzegovina -Advocacy activities with the local authorities in the City of Mostar resulted in placing a new bus station next to the project community and co-financing up to 50% of the amount granted by the REF in 3 projects from 2015 to 2019 with their full support in the projects implementation. -At population level, during the REF activity in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the following beneficiaries have received support: over 600 children in ECD and preschool activities, over 5,000 children in primary education, over 500 students in secondary education, over 10,000 parents and 13 university students.
North Macedonia -During the 2009-2019 period, the state budget for the REF pre-school project increased from 0% to 60%-80% thanks to a partnership between REF and Ministry of Labour and Social Policy (MoLSP). Roma people from 21 municipalities benefited from this budget allocation. -From 2018 onwards, all Roma children in pre-school age (4-6 years old) living in 21 municipalities, where both parents are unemployed or are from single-parent families can be enrolled in the integrated state kindergartens free of charge, and their daily attendance is paid by the state budget-MoLSP budget (25 Euro per month from September till June every year). -A new integrated kindergarten was opened in the Village of Crnik (Municipality of Pehcevo), where all kids (Roma, Turkish and Macedonian) a total of 35 children of pre-school age i.e. 3 to 6 years old, are enrolled in the kindergarten free of charge and their daily attendance paid every year by the municipality of Pehcevo and the Ministry of LSP) as from 2010-2011. -1000 scholarships for Roma secondary students are granted every year by the MoES through the State Ministry of ES budget. -Out of the primary school Roma children (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th grade enrolled in the Primary education per school year in 49 primary schools in 16 municipalities (5,800), 3,200 of them are tutored through REF, Roma NGOs or the Ministry of Education and Science Project, i.e. 55 percent of all students during the 2011-2021 period. -Out of the secondary education Roma students enrolled per school year (around 1,600), around 1.000 receive scholarships and are tutored through support by REF and the Ministry of Education and Science project i.e. 62,5 percent of all students during the 2010-2021 period. -Out of all the tertiary education Roma students enrolled in higher education per academic year (around 250), approximately 150 receive scholarships, are tutored, trained, etc. through REF and REF's partner organisation, or 60 percent - 2005-2021 period.
Albania -A new strategy for social inclusion was prepared by the Ministry of Youth and Social Welfare in 2015, with an action plan focusing on improving the situation of Roma and Egyptian people (2015-2020). REF made comments and recommendations on education, registration, anti-trafficking and health, based on findings and lessons learned in the past 10 years. -During 2016 the Council of Ministers approved a decision providing scholarships for high school Roma students who study in professional high schools. -REF, together with its partner organisation in adult education RWRC, advocated to make the adult education legislative framework more beneficial to Roma and Egyptian adults and in 2018 the New Law on Adult Education gave the interested candidates to the adult part-time program, that lacked previous formal studies, the possibility to take a test and be registered to the class equivalent to their actual level of knowledge. This motivated many Roma and Egyptian youth to register with the program. -REF and its partners participated in the discussions concerning new laws that influence the chance to a better life for Roma, such as: the Law on Social Housing: 6 Decisions of Council of Ministers were developed; the Law on Social Enterprises: 3 by-laws that were endorsed; the Law on Social Care; Public consultations on the drafting of the Youth Law in Albania took place. -During 2020 REF worked closely with the Albanian Government and local authorities to discuss and provide free access to internet and technology to pupils and students in major cities and remote areas.
Montenegro -The main REF focus was on primary education, and it was implemented the program of mediators in the community. This program was adopted by the government which is still financing the program. However, after the government took over the program some standards were changed. The municipality requires that there are at least 70 Roma children, in order to employ a mediator. Furthermore the mediator needs to have completed at least secondary education. At the beginning of the program this was a challenge for Roma community due to a lack of persons who had completed secondary education. Today this has changed but they are facing the problems due to the small number of Roma children in many other municipalities, and the high number of children that the mediator has to cover.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
